threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' like it’s a subway. Local folks just call it the ‘overground’ if they’re being polite.
Last night on the 59, saw two guys arguing over who had the worst taste in music; one swore by 90s pop, the other raved about garage. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy washing his bike in the fountain at Hasenheide, I knew I had found my place in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find kebab shops serving homemade döner with thick, fluffy bread that's a treat late at night. Nonexistent elsewhere!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who’s local by their reaction to the Muni delays. Newcomers just complain; longtime residents automatically check their watch and adjust plans.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a dog calmly sitting on the tracks at Civic Center, like it owned the place. Typical San Francisco vibe right there.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just walk into a bar and order a 'tapa' without being specific. 'Tapa' is a vague term here; it's all about the details.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion at how long the metro can be delayed, still expecting punctuality like in Germany.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when you see the 'Not in Service' sign on a Tube train. You think it's broken, but really, it’s just the way of life here.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken on the 35 last night; turns out the guy next to me had a full takeout tucked away. Smell was better company than him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a bus the other day, and the driver hopped out to grab a snack from the Kiosk, all while the passengers just waited. Classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that serves drinks in old soup cans. It’s a quirky twist that blends nostalgia with nightlife.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local if they know to avoid the 14-Mission during rush hour. Tourists just think it’s an Uber problem.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo hop on the 31 at Civic Center after a wedding. He smiled and said, 'Nothing says love like a crowded bus ride home.' Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all bohemian charm, but many locals avoid it during festival time—too many drumming tourists drown out our evenings.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a 'café con leche' but pronounce it like it's a spell from Harry Potter. It's always 'café con letche' around here.
